steps.title: Start with an empty canvas
steps.body: New-BGInfoBackground sets the size and paints one colour. Without it, PowerBGInfo draws on -FilePath or on the wallpaper that is already set, and never on its own earlier output.

steps.title: Gradient
steps.body: Two colours blend across the canvas.

steps.title: Glows
steps.body: Soft radial light at relative positions, so it lands in the same place at every resolution.

steps.title: Pattern
steps.body: A grid on top. Dots work the same way.

steps.title: Name the machine
steps.body: Labels and name and value pairs form the text block in the top-left corner. -BuiltinValue HostName, OSName or IPv4Address read the machine the script runs on; this page uses fixed values so anyone can reproduce the render.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
    Gradient = '#0B3B46', '#050A14'
    Glow = @(
        New-BGInfoBackgroundGlow -X 0.85 -Y 0.1 -Radius 0.6 -Color '#2DD4BF40'
        New-BGInfoBackgroundGlow -X 0.05 -Y 0.95 -Radius 0.5 -Color '#3B82F633'
    )
    Pattern = 'Grid'
    PatternSpacing = 64
}

New-BGInfo -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3' -Color '#2DD4BF' -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'WS-FIN-0042' -Color White -FontSize 64 -Bold
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'User' -Value 'CONTOSO\anowak'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value 'Windows 11 Enterprise'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value '10.20.4.37'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'
} -Color '#94A3B8' -ValueColor White -FontSize 18 -SpaceX 64 -SpaceY 56 `
    -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'

New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3' -Color '#2DD4BF' -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'WS-FIN-0042' -Color White -FontSize 64 -Bold

    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'
} -Color '#94A3B8' -ValueColor White -FontSize 18 -SpaceX 64 -SpaceY 56 `
    -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'

steps.title: Pick a theme preset
steps.body: -Theme Aurora gives the text, the panels and the backdrop one look, so the hand-picked colours and the background layers go. Parameters you set still win, and -ThemeMode Light gives the light pair.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
}

New-BGInfo -Theme Aurora -ThemeMode Dark -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3' -Accent -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'WS-FIN-0042' -FontSize 64 -Bold
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'User' -Value 'CONTOSO\anowak'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value 'Windows 11 Enterprise'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value '10.20.4.37'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'

steps.title: Add the first chart
steps.body: A chart panel placed by anchor and offsets, the way PowerBGInfo has always placed them. It picks up the theme's panel, type and series colour without a single colour parameter.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
}

New-BGInfo -Theme Aurora -ThemeMode Dark -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3' -Accent -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'WS-FIN-0042' -FontSize 64 -Bold
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'User' -Value 'CONTOSO\anowak'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value 'Windows 11 Enterprise'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value '10.20.4.37'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'

    New-BGInfoChart -Title 'CPU' -Kind Area -Values 12, 18, 25, 22, 30, 27 `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory `
        -Anchor TopRight -OffsetX 64 -OffsetY 56 -Width 460 -Height 240
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'

steps.title: Let regions do the layout
steps.body: -Region Right stacks panels in a column and -Region Bottom shares a band. Nobody computes widths, the taskbar stays clear, and the layout follows the screen size; the region renders further down show it at ultrawide and portrait sizes.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
}

New-BGInfo -Theme Aurora -ThemeMode Dark -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3' -Accent -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'WS-FIN-0042' -FontSize 64 -Bold
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'User' -Value 'CONTOSO\anowak'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value 'Windows 11 Enterprise'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value '10.20.4.37'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'

    New-BGInfoChart -Title 'CPU' -Kind Area -Values 12, 18, 25, 22, 30, 27 `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory `
        -Region Right
    New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Memory' -Value 86 -Unit '%' `
        -Caption 'of 32 GB' -Height 150

    New-BGInfoChart -Region Bottom -Title 'Volumes used' -Kind ProgressBar `
        -Values 63, 93 -Labels 'C: System', 'D: Data' -Maximum 100 `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false `
        -NoHistory
    New-BGInfoChart -Region Bottom -Title 'Network' -Kind Line `
        -Values 120, 180, 160, 220, 260, 240 -ValueSuffix ' Mbps' -NoHistory
    New-BGInfoList -Region Bottom -Title 'This week' -Item @(
        @{ Text = 'Month-end close'; Checked = $false; Value = 'Fri' }
        @{ Text = 'Backups verified'; Checked = $true; Value = '02:10' }
    )
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'

steps.title: Add thresholds
steps.body: Warning and critical thresholds turn the memory card amber and the D: bar red by themselves, using the theme's status colours.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
}

New-BGInfo -Theme Aurora -ThemeMode Dark -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3' -Accent -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name 'WS-FIN-0042' -FontSize 64 -Bold

    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value 'Windows 11 Enterprise'
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value '10.20.4.37'

    New-BGInfoChart -Title 'CPU' -Kind Area -Values 12, 18, 25, 22, 30, 27 `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory `
        -Region Right
    New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Memory' -Value 86 -Unit '%' `
        -Caption 'of 32 GB' -Height 150 `

    )

steps.title: Bring your own data
steps.body: The values move into one function, Invoke-BGInfoDataSource runs it with a time limit and a fallback, and the drawing code only reads $data. The wallpaper looks the same; now it is yours.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-MyWallpaperData {
    # Sample values. Each comment names a live source for the same value.
    [pscustomobject] @{
        Team = 'FINANCE · FLOOR 3'
        Name = 'WS-FIN-0042'                # $env:COMPUTERNAME
        User = 'CONTOSO\anowak'             # Win32_ComputerSystem.UserName
        Windows = 'Windows 11 Enterprise'   # Win32_OperatingSystem.Caption
        IPv4 = '10.20.4.37'                 # Get-NetIPAddress
        Cpu = 12, 18, 25, 22, 30, 27        # Get-Counter, or your monitoring
        Memory = 86                         # Win32_OperatingSystem, % in use
        # Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter, % used per volume
        Volumes = [ordered] @{ 'C: System' = 63; 'D: Data' = 93 }
        Network = 120, 180, 160, 220, 260, 240
        Tasks = @(
            @{ Text = 'Month-end close'; Checked = $false; Value = 'Fri' }
            @{ Text = 'Backups verified'; Checked = $true; Value = '02:10' }
        )
    }
}

# What the wallpaper shows when the source fails or runs out of time.
$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Team = 'STATUS UNAVAILABLE'; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    User = 'unknown'; Windows = 'unknown'; IPv4 = 'unknown'
    Cpu = @(0); Memory = 0; Volumes = @{ 'C:' = 0 }; Network = @(0)
    Tasks = @(@{ Text = 'Status unknown'; Checked = $false })
}
$source = @{
    Name = 'Wallpaper data'
    TimeoutSeconds = 10
    ScriptBlock = ${function:Get-MyWallpaperData}
    Default = $fallback
}
$data = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $data
$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
}

New-BGInfo -Theme Aurora -ThemeMode Dark -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $data.Team -Accent -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $data.Name -FontSize 64 -Bold
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'User' -Value $data.User
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value $data.Windows
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value $data.IPv4
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'

    New-BGInfoChart -Title 'CPU' -Kind Area -Values $data.Cpu `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory `
        -Region Right
    New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Memory' -Unit '%' `
        -Value $data.Memory -Caption 'of 32 GB' -Height 150 `
        -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90

    New-BGInfoChart -Region Bottom -Title 'Volumes used' -Kind ProgressBar `
        -Values @($data.Volumes.Values) -Labels @($data.Volumes.Keys) `
        -Maximum 100 `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false `
        -NoHistory -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
    New-BGInfoChart -Region Bottom -Title 'Network' -Kind Line `
        -Values $data.Network -ValueSuffix ' Mbps' -NoHistory
    New-BGInfoList -Region Bottom -Title 'This week' -Item $data.Tasks
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'
#endregion

steps.title: When the source does not answer
steps.body: The same script with a source that hangs. Invoke-BGInfoDataSource stops waiting after ten seconds, writes a warning and returns the fallback, and the wallpaper still renders.
steps.script:
param([string] $OutputDirectory = "$env:TEMP\PowerBGInfo")

#region Data: your logic goes here
function Get-MyWallpaperData {
    # A source that never answers: a CMDB that is down, a share that hangs.
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 60
    [pscustomobject] @{ Team = 'too late' }
}

# What the wallpaper shows when the source fails or runs out of time.
$fallback = [pscustomobject] @{
    Team = 'STATUS UNAVAILABLE'; Name = $env:COMPUTERNAME
    User = 'unknown'; Windows = 'unknown'; IPv4 = 'unknown'
    Cpu = @(0); Memory = 0; Volumes = @{ 'C:' = 0 }; Network = @(0)
    Tasks = @(@{ Text = 'Status unknown'; Checked = $false })
}
$source = @{
    Name = 'Wallpaper data'
    TimeoutSeconds = 10
    ScriptBlock = ${function:Get-MyWallpaperData}
    Default = $fallback
}
$data = Invoke-BGInfoDataSource @source
#endregion

#region Presentation: reads only $data
$backdrop = @{
    Width = 1920
    Height = 1080
}

New-BGInfo -Theme Aurora -ThemeMode Dark -Target File {
    New-BGInfoBackground @backdrop

    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $data.Team -Accent -FontWeight 700
    New-BGInfoLabel -Name $data.Name -FontSize 64 -Bold
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'User' -Value $data.User
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Windows' -Value $data.Windows
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'IP address' -Value $data.IPv4
    New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Support' -Value 'ext. 4357'

    New-BGInfoChart -Title 'CPU' -Kind Area -Values $data.Cpu `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoHistory `
        -Region Right
    New-BGInfoMetric -Region Right -Label 'Memory' -Unit '%' `
        -Value $data.Memory -Caption 'of 32 GB' -Height 150 `
        -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90

    New-BGInfoChart -Region Bottom -Title 'Volumes used' -Kind ProgressBar `
        -Values @($data.Volumes.Values) -Labels @($data.Volumes.Keys) `
        -Maximum 100 `
        -ValueSuffix ' %' -NoProgressHandles -ShowLatestValue:$false `
        -NoHistory -WarningThreshold 80 -CriticalThreshold 90
    New-BGInfoChart -Region Bottom -Title 'Network' -Kind Line `
        -Values $data.Network -ValueSuffix ' Mbps' -NoHistory
    New-BGInfoList -Region Bottom -Title 'This week' -Item $data.Tasks
} -ConfigurationDirectory $OutputDirectory -OutputFileName 'wallpaper.png'
#endregion

sources.label: CIM and WMI
sources.body: Operating system, memory, uptime and fixed disks from Get-CimInstance. Read-only, and no module to install.

sources.label: Registry
sources.body: The Windows release and build, and values your build or asset process wrote under its own key.

sources.label: Active Directory
sources.body: The signed-in user's department and title, and the computer's description and owner, from the ActiveDirectory module.

sources.label: REST API
sources.body: A CMDB or ticketing API through Invoke-RestMethod. The function runs in its own runspace, so it gets the computer name through -ArgumentList.

sources.label: Monitoring export
sources.body: JSON and CSV files that a monitoring tool already exports, read with ConvertFrom-Json and Import-Csv.

sources.label: Swap a built-in helper
sources.body: Get-BGInfoSystemInfo returns plain data. A function of your own that returns the same property names replaces it without touching the layout.
